# Reader Guide and Prerequisites {.unnumbered}

*Physical AI Systems* is written for advanced undergraduate students, graduate researchers, and practicing systems engineers who wish to build machines that safely couple learned intelligence to physical matter and energy.

Because Physical AI bridges disciplines that are traditionally separated in university curricula—machine learning, embedded systems, real-time operating systems, and classical dynamics—the text is designed to be intellectually self-contained wherever these fields intersect. You do not need dual doctorates in deep learning and mechanical engineering to read this book. All companion firmware harnesses, hardware schematics, and laboratory benchmarks are hosted online at [`physical.mlsysbook.ai`](https://physical.mlsysbook.ai).

## The Technical Baseline

To engage deeply with the concepts and laboratory milestones in this text, you should be comfortable with a focused set of software and mathematical foundations:

* **Programming & Systems:** Fluency in Python and introductory familiarity with C or C++. You should be comfortable reading low-level code, navigating structs and pointers, and reasoning about the fundamental difference between static memory and dynamic heap allocation.
* **Machine Learning Intuition:** Familiarity with neural network inference (such as PyTorch or ONNX Runtime) and tensor representations. You should understand that learned models produce approximate, stochastic proposals rather than deterministic guarantees.
* **Foundational Physics & Mathematics:** Core Newtonian mechanics ($F = ma$, kinetic momentum $\mathbf{p} = m\mathbf{v}$, and kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$), basic linear algebra (vectors, matrices, and 3D coordinate transformations), and single-variable differential calculus (rates of change, velocity, acceleration, and jerk).

## Disciplinary Reading Pathways

Readers approach Physical AI from different engineering traditions. To maximize the value of this text, we suggest specific points of emphasis based on your background:

* **For Machine Learning Practitioners:** Focus on the physical consequences of computation. Digital models operate under the illusion that time pauses during deliberation. Pay close attention to @sec-body (tail latency metrology and dynamic stopping kinematics), @sec-enforcement (real-time Control Barrier Function safety enforcers), and @sec-placement (unified memory bus contention and heterogeneous silicon placement).
* **For Embedded Systems & Silicon Architects:** Focus on hosting stochastic, high-capacity representations without sacrificing determinism. Pay close attention to @sec-perception (spatial affordance tokens and zero-copy DMA), @sec-intent (vision-language model grounding and expiring intent leases), and @sec-planning (diffusion action chunking and $\mathcal{C}^2$ differential jerk continuity).
* **For Roboticists & Control Engineers:** Focus on closing the physical loop around learned models. Pay close attention to @sec-boundary (the Proposal–Permission Privilege Split), @sec-nervous (multi-rate asynchronous execution runtimes), @sec-intervention (policy data integrity and supervisor overrides), and @sec-release (Claim-Argument-Evidence safety cases for defensible release).

## What the Book Builds from First Principles

Where specialized concepts are required, this book develops them from first principles, establishing clean systems mechanisms rather than assuming graduate coursework:

* **The Proposal–Permission Privilege Split:** We formalize the heterogeneous runtime contract separating unprivileged cognitive proposals (on host processors) from privileged real-time safety supervisors (on bare-metal microcontrollers).
* **Control Barrier Functions (CBFs):** We introduce forward-invariant safe sets ($h(x) \ge 0$) and dynamic stopping projections through intuitive Newtonian stopping physics, without requiring prior graduate control theory.
* **Multi-Rate Asynchronous Runtimes:** We derive the lock-free data structures and memory layouts needed to interface 1 Hz vision-language reasoning, 20–50 Hz trajectory generation, and 1 kHz bare-metal motor reflexes.
* **Spatial Coordinate Frame Trees:** We trace how visual tokens are grounded in three-dimensional $SE(3)$ coordinate frames and how discrete waypoint predictions are smoothed to eliminate destructive gearbox jerk.
* **Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE) Assurance Cases:** We teach System-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA) and evidence-backed safety dossiers as concrete, verifiable engineering deliverables.

## What We Deliberately Omit

To maintain a relentless focus on the core systems question—*what must the surrounding system guarantee before an unverified learned proposal may produce a physical consequence?*—we deliberately exclude traditional academic baggage:

* **Exhaustive Robotic Kinematic Derivations:** We do not derive pages of multi-link Denavit-Hartenberg parameter tables or closed-form manipulator Jacobians. Kinematic boundaries are treated as verifiable reachability and collision envelopes.
* **Disembodied Deep Learning Theory:** We do not probe loss landscape geometry, non-convex optimization dynamics, or cloud cluster scaling behind glass.
* **Brittle Cloud Prompt-Chaining Frameworks:** We do not cover fragile cloud LLM wrapper libraries or conversational web scrapers. All intelligence in this text is physically grounded, local to the machine, and accountable to physical laws.
